quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #2
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: Signal at least 100 feet before changing lanes to pass. Make sure there is no oncoming traffic.
Use your mirrors and look over your left shoulder to check your blind spot when passing left.
When passing, wait until you see both headlights of the other car in your rearview mirror before returning to your lane.

questions.explanation: When passing, always signal at least 100 feet before you change lanes. Always check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Wait until you see both headlights of the other car in your rearview mirror before returning to your lane.

questions.question: Traffic signs and pavement markings:

options.text: Must be followed only when other traffic is present.
Must be followed only when a police officer is present.

questions.explanation: Pavement markings, traffic signals, and signs control traffic flow. They tell drivers about road conditions and help guide them safely. You must always obey traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings.

questions.question: Fog reduces visibility of vehicles, pedestrians, and traffic signals. When driving in fog, you should:

options.text: Drive carefully and reduce your speed.
Not use your high beam headlights.
Use low beam headlights to see the road and objects better.

questions.explanation: Fog makes it hard to see vehicles, pedestrians, and traffic signals. When driving in fog, drive carefully at a reduced speed. Do not use high beam headlights. Low beams work better to light the road and objects ahead in foggy conditions.

questions.question: As you approach an intersection, the traffic light changes from green to yellow. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to pass through before the red light.
Be ready to stop in the middle of the intersection.
Be ready to stop before the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop before the intersection.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means the red light is coming soon. Be ready to stop for the red light if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: When you hear a fire engine siren behind you, you must:

options.text: Pull over to the side of the road and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear an emergency vehicle siren, pull over to the curb or side of the road and stop.

questions.question: This road sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign warns of a steep downhill grade ahead.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should use your:
questions.explanation: In fog, use your low beam headlights and fog lights if your vehicle has them. High beams bounce light off the fog and back into your eyes, making visibility worse.

questions.question: At a four-way stop:

options.text: The driver who arrives first has the right-of-way.
The driver who arrives last has the right-of-way.
One driver should continue without stopping.
One driver should wave others ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver who arrives first has the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: At four-way stops, all vehicles must stop. The first vehicle to reach the intersection goes first. If two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the right goes first.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light mean?
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means drive carefully and stay alert.

questions.question: Drinking alcohol and driving is:

options.text: Safe if you have only had a few drinks.

questions.explanation: Driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs is a serious safety problem. You cannot drive safely when you drink or use drugs. It puts you and everyone on the road at risk.

questions.question: When you see other drivers acting or reacting with anger, what should you do?
questions.explanation: When other drivers are angry, move away from them. Do not look at them or make gestures that could upset them. Slow down, change lanes, or do whatever is safe to get away from danger.

questions.question: When you see a flashing yellow light, what should you do?
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light warns you of danger ahead. Slow down and be careful.

questions.question: If your car breaks down on a highway, what should you do?

options.text: Stay in your car and wait for help.
Turn on your hazard lights to warn other drivers.
Honk your horn at passing cars.
Flash your headlights at oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your hazard lights to warn other drivers.
questions.explanation: If your car breaks down on the highway, turn on your hazard lights. Carefully move your car as far off the road as possible. Raise your hood so other drivers know your car is broken down.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: A highway entrance ramp is ahead.

questions.explanation: This sign tells you that the right lane will end ahead.

questions.question: When you see a flashing red traffic light, what should you do?

options.text: Go through if no other cars are coming.
Keep driving because you have the right-of-way.
Stop only if a police officer is there.
Treat it like a stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat it like a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light is used at dangerous intersections. Treat it the same as a stop sign.

questions.question: Drivers who have had alcohol are:

options.text: Always aware of the risks they are taking.
Unable to control their body, mind, or vehicle properly.
Better drivers because they are more careful.

questions.correctAnswerText: Unable to control their body, mind, or vehicle properly.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your thinking, harms your vision, reduces focus, and makes you react slower. It is never safe to drink and drive.

questions.question: When you see a blind person with a white cane or guide dog, you should:

options.text: Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: When you see a blind person with a white cane or guide dog, slow down and let them cross. Be ready to stop to keep them safe.

questions.question: If a police officer is directing traffic at a working traffic light, you should:

options.text: Do what the cars next to you are doing.

questions.explanation: Traffic lights help keep traffic moving safely. You must obey them, but if a police officer is directing traffic, follow the officer's directions instead.

questions.question: You should look over your shoulder to check your blind spot when:

options.text: Pulling toward or away from a curb.

questions.explanation: Check your blind spot every time you change your car's position. This includes turning, changing lanes, and pulling toward or away from a curb.

questions.question: If a police officer stops you, what should you do?

options.text: Unbuckle your seat belt and lower your window.
Have your paperwork ready before the officer gets to your car.
Stay in your car with your hands on the steering wheel and wait for the officer.
Get out and walk toward the patrol car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your car with your hands on the steering wheel and wait for the officer.
questions.explanation: Keep your hands on the wheel when stopped. Tell passengers to keep their hands visible too. Stay in your car unless the officer asks you to get out. Wait for the officer to ask for your license, registration, and insurance.

questions.question: When driving on slippery roads, you should:

options.text: Take turns more slowly than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take turns more slowly than usual.
questions.explanation: Slippery roads are always dangerous. Turns and curves are especially risky. Slow down more than usual when taking turns on wet or icy roads.

questions.question: To drive safely at night, you should:

options.text: Not drive if you are tired.
Make sure your headlights work properly.

questions.explanation: At night, you cannot see as well. Do all of these things to stay safe and protect other drivers.

questions.question: You notice a vehicle defect that may affect safe operation. You should:

options.text: Fix the defect as soon as possible.
Fix the defect when you can afford it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fix the defect as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: Any defect that affects safe operation must be fixed right away. Do not drive the vehicle until it is fixed.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They tell you about road conditions ahead. This sign warns you that traffic may come from the opposite direction.

questions.question: When approaching railroad tracks, you should:

options.text: Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop.
Speed up to cross before the gate comes down.
Ignore how many tracks you need to cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: At railroad tracks, look both ways, listen for trains, slow down, and be ready to stop. Watch for trains or other vehicles on the tracks.

questions.question: When a school bus stops with its stop arm out, you should:

options.text: Honk and pass on the left.
Keep driving when children finish exiting.

questions.explanation: When a school bus shows its stop signal, you must stop completely. Do not move until the stop arm is raised.

questions.question: How can alcohol affect your driving?

options.text: It makes you feel falsely confident.

questions.explanation: Alcohol affects the part of your brain that controls good judgment and self-control. It slows your reaction time, hurts your balance, and makes it hard to judge distance. You may feel overly confident, which is dangerous.

questions.question: Stop lines are white lines painted across traffic lanes at:
questions.explanation: Stop lines are white lines at intersections and pedestrian crosswalks. They show exactly where you must stop.

questions.question: Which of the following must you obey first?
questions.explanation: A police officer's directions come before signs, signals, and road markings. Police officers, firefighters, and school crossing guards can direct traffic.

questions.question: Which of the following increases crash risk for distracted drivers?
questions.explanation: Using a cell phone, radio, or CD player while driving takes your attention off the road. All of these can cause crashes.

questions.question: Checking your blind spot by turning your head before changing lanes, leaving a curb, or merging into traffic is:

options.text: Not necessary if you use the rearview mirror.

questions.explanation: Check your blind spots by looking over your shoulder before changing lanes. Do not rely only on your mirrors.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Make sure the lane is clear before entering.

questions.explanation: Signal before changing lanes. Turn your head and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Make sure the lane is clear before moving into it.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, you should:

options.text: Stay calm and move out of the aggressive driver's way.
Flash your lights to show the driver is wrong.
React with your own aggressive driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay calm and move out of the aggressive driver's way.
questions.explanation: Stay calm and get out of an aggressive driver's way. Do not try to get even with them. Reacting can make the situation more dangerous.

questions.question: You should honk your horn when you:

options.text: See a child about to run into the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: See a child about to run into the street.
questions.explanation: Use your horn as a warning when you think a driver or pedestrian does not see you. For example, honk if a child is about to run in front of your vehicle.

questions.question: A seat belt should be adjusted so that it:

options.text: Fits snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
Stops the seat belt buzzer or light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fits snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
questions.explanation: Lap belts should fit snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen. Shoulder belts should be comfortable with room for your fist between the belt and your chest.

questions.question: Alcohol causes:
questions.explanation: Even a small amount of alcohol harms your vision, judgment, concentration, and coordination.

questions.question: Mixing alcohol with drugs can:

options.text: Decrease the effects of the drugs and alcohol.
Increase the effects of both the drugs and alcohol.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase the effects of both the drugs and alcohol.
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol and drugs increases the effects of both. It is unsafe to drive after consuming alcohol or drugs. It is even more dangerous when combined.

questions.question: You may not park:

options.text: On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.
Within 12 inches of the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to park on a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane. When parking on the street, stay within 12 inches of the edge of the road.

questions.question: Highway hypnosis can result from:

options.text: Staring at the roadway for long periods of time.
Too much sleep the night before your trip.

questions.correctAnswerText: Staring at the roadway for long periods of time.
questions.explanation: Highway hypnosis happens when you stare straight ahead and stop looking around. You can zone out and miss traffic slowing or stopping ahead of you.

questions.question: The only way to reduce your blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is to:

options.text: Allow your body time to remove the alcohol.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow your body time to remove the alcohol.
questions.explanation: Only time reduces your BAC. Coffee, exercise, and cold showers cannot lower your BAC or make you sober. They may keep you awake, but they do not change your BAC.
